q: Two sibling elements have margin-bottom: 30px and margin-top: 20px. What is the actual space between them?
options: 50px — margins add together
30px — the larger margin wins due to margin collapsing
20px — the smaller margin wins
25px — the average of both margins
explain: Vertical margins between adjacent block elements collapse into a single margin equal to the larger of the two. This is called margin collapsing and only happens vertically not horizontally.

q: You use flexbox and items are stretching to fill the container height. You don't want this. What do you set?
options: flex-shrink: 0 on each item
align-items: flex-start on the container
justify-content: flex-start on the container
flex-wrap: nowrap on the container
explain: The default align-items value is stretch which makes items fill the container's cross axis. Setting align-items: flex-start makes items only as tall as their content.

q: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items in flexbox?
options: justify-content aligns vertically, align-items aligns horizontally
justify-content aligns along the main axis, align-items aligns along the cross axis
They are identical but justify-content is for grid and align-items is for flexbox
align-items only works when flex-wrap is enabled
explain: justify-content distributes items along the main axis (row direction by default). align-items aligns items along the cross axis (column direction by default).

q: You want a grid with 3 equal columns that adapt to the container width. What is the cleanest way?
options: grid-template-columns: 33% 33% 33%
grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)
grid-template-columns: auto auto auto
columns: 3
explain: 1fr means one fraction of available space. repeat(3, 1fr) creates 3 equal columns that share all available space. Using percentages can cause overflow due to gaps.

q: What is the difference between Flexbox and Grid?
options: Flexbox is for older browsers, Grid is modern
Flexbox is one-dimensional for rows or columns, Grid is two-dimensional for rows and columns simultaneously
Grid only works for page layouts, Flexbox works for components
They are identical with different syntax
explain: Flexbox controls layout in one direction at a time — either row or column. Grid controls both dimensions simultaneously making it better for complex two-dimensional layouts.

q: You want a sticky header that stays at the top while scrolling but only within its parent container. What position do you use?
options: position: fixed
position: sticky with top: 0
position: absolute with top: 0
position: relative with overflow: hidden
explain: position: sticky behaves like relative until the element reaches the threshold then sticks like fixed — but only within its parent container. position: fixed sticks to the viewport regardless of parent.

q: You define a CSS variable as --brand-color: #FE5C01. How do you use it?
options: color: var(brand-color)
color: var(--brand-color)
color: $brand-color
color: @brand-color
explain: CSS custom properties are accessed with the var() function. The property name must include the double dash prefix. This is different from Sass variables which use $.

q: You want a transition when a button changes color on hover. What CSS do you add to the button?
options: animation: color 0.3s ease on :hover
transition: background-color 0.3s ease on the base button style
transform: color 0.3s on the button
hover-transition: 0.3s on the button
explain: transition is added to the element's base style not the :hover state. It tells the browser to animate changes to the specified property over time when any state change occurs.

q: You use transform: translateX(100px). Does this affect surrounding elements?
options: Yes it pushes neighboring elements to the right
No transform moves the element visually but does not affect document flow
Only if the element is position: relative
Yes it updates the element's margin
explain: CSS transforms move elements visually but do not affect layout. The element's original space is preserved in the document flow so neighbors are not pushed around.

q: You want to perfectly center a div both horizontally and vertically inside its parent. What is the modern one-liner?
options: margin: auto on the child
display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center on the parent
position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 50% on the child
text-align: center; vertical-align: middle on the parent
explain: Flexbox centering is the cleanest modern approach. Setting both align-items and justify-content to center on the parent centers the child in both dimensions.

q: What is a pseudo-element and how does it differ from a pseudo-class?
options: They are the same thing with different syntax
Pseudo-elements style a specific part of an element, pseudo-classes style elements based on state
Pseudo-classes use :: and pseudo-elements use :
Pseudo-elements only work on block elements
explain: Pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after target parts of an element or create virtual content. Pseudo-classes like :hover and :focus target elements based on state or position.

q: You use ::before to add content before an element. The content does not appear. What is likely missing?
options: The element needs position: relative
The content property must be set even if empty
::before only works on block elements
You need to set display: block on the pseudo-element
explain: The content property is required for ::before and ::after to render. Even if you want no text you must set content: '' for the pseudo-element to appear.

q: You want a layout where items wrap to the next line when there is not enough space. What flexbox property enables this?
options: flex-direction: wrap
flex-wrap: wrap
flex-flow: wrap
overflow: wrap
explain: flex-wrap: wrap allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines. By default flex-wrap is nowrap which forces all items onto one line even if they overflow.

q: What does the CSS property will-change do?
options: It tells the browser which CSS properties will change soon so it can optimize rendering
It prevents CSS properties from changing
It schedules a CSS animation to run later
It marks an element for JavaScript manipulation
explain: will-change hints to the browser that specific properties will animate so it can promote the element to its own compositor layer. Overusing it wastes memory — only apply it when needed.

q: You want a grid item to span 2 columns. What property do you set on the item?
options: grid-column-span: 2
grid-column: span 2
column-span: 2
flex-span: 2
explain: grid-column: span 2 tells a grid item to span 2 column tracks. You can also use grid-column: 1 / 3 to specify start and end lines explicitly.

q: What is the difference between min-width and max-width in responsive design?
options: min-width targets large screens, max-width targets small screens
min-width applies styles from that breakpoint up, max-width applies styles up to that breakpoint
They are identical — just mobile-first vs desktop-first naming
max-width is deprecated in favor of min-width
explain: min-width is mobile-first — styles apply from that width upward. max-width is desktop-first — styles apply up to that width. min-width is the modern recommended approach.

q: You notice a layout shift when a web font loads. What CSS property helps prevent this?
options: font-display: swap
font-loading: prevent-shift
text-rendering: stable
font-delay: none
explain: font-display: swap tells the browser to show a fallback font immediately and swap to the web font when it loads. Other values like optional can prevent layout shift entirely by not swapping if the font loads too slowly.

q: What does the clip-path property do?
options: Clips the element's overflow content
Defines a visible region and hides everything outside that shape
Clips the element's border radius
Prevents the element from being selected
explain: clip-path creates a clipping region using shapes like circle, polygon, or SVG paths. Everything outside the region is hidden. Useful for creative shapes and image masks.

q: You want CSS styles to only apply inside a specific component without affecting global styles. What approach do you use?
options: Use !important on all component styles
CSS Modules or scoped styles that auto-generate unique class names
Prefix all selectors with the component name manually
Use inline styles for everything
explain: CSS Modules automatically scope styles to the component by generating unique class names at build time. This prevents style leakage without manual prefixing or specificity hacks.

q: You set opacity: 0 on an element. Can the user still interact with it?
options: No — opacity: 0 removes all interactivity
Yes — the element is invisible but still occupies space and receives events
Only if pointer-events: auto is set
It depends on the browser
explain: opacity: 0 makes an element invisible but it still exists in the layout and receives mouse events. Use pointer-events: none to also disable interactions, or visibility: hidden.

q: What is a stacking context and when is one created?
options: A CSS feature that stacks multiple backgrounds on one element
An isolated layer where z-index values are compared — created by position with z-index, opacity less than 1, or transform
The order in which CSS files are loaded
A flexbox feature for ordering items
explain: A stacking context is a self-contained layer. z-index only competes within the same stacking context. New ones are created by position + z-index, opacity < 1, transform, filter and others.

q: You want an element to grow and fill available space in a flex container. What property do you set on the item?
options: flex-grow: 0
flex: 1 or flex-grow: 1
width: 100%
align-self: stretch
explain: flex-grow: 1 tells the item to take up any available space in the container. flex: 1 is shorthand for flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1, flex-basis: 0.

q: What does the gap property do in CSS Grid and Flexbox?
options: Adds space between the container and its children
Adds space between items without needing margins on each item
Sets the minimum space items need before wrapping
gap only works in Grid not Flexbox
explain: gap adds consistent space between grid or flex items. It is cleaner than adding margins to each item because it doesn't add space on the outer edges.

q: You want to animate an element smoothly. Which properties should you animate for best performance?
options: width and height — they are the most common
transform and opacity — they are GPU accelerated and don't trigger layout
margin and padding — they affect spacing directly
color and background-color — they are lightweight
explain: transform and opacity are handled by the GPU compositor and do not trigger layout or paint. Animating width, height, margin or padding causes expensive layout recalculations on every frame.

q: You use position: absolute on a child but it positions relative to the page not the parent. What is wrong?
options: Absolute positioning always uses the page as reference
The parent needs a position other than static set on it
You need to set overflow: hidden on the parent
Absolute positioning only works inside flex containers
explain: Absolutely positioned elements look for the nearest positioned ancestor. If no ancestor has position set they use the initial containing block. Add position: relative to the parent to contain the child.
